title: How to Slice Fresh Ginger Thin for Stir‑Fry and Tea Using a Mandoline
meta_description: Learn how to slice fresh ginger thin for stir-fry and tea using a mandoline, a game-changing kitchen tool.
html:
Thin sliced fresh ginger is a staple in many Asian dishes and is also a popular ingredient in herbal teas. But slicing it can be a challenge, especially if you don't have the right tool. Enter the Mandoline Slicer, a restaurant-quality mandoline that can help you achieve even, thin slices of ginger with ease.

Here's a step-by-step guide on how to slice fresh ginger thin using a mandoline:

Choosing the Right Fresh Ginger

Before we dive into the slicing process, it's essential to choose the right fresh ginger. Look for ginger that's firm, with no soft spots or wrinkles. The skin should be a deep orange or yellow color, depending on the variety.

You can find fresh ginger at most supermarkets or Asian markets. Choose a piece that's about 1-2 inches in diameter and 4-6 inches long.

Preparing the Ginger

Once you've chosen your fresh ginger, it's time to prepare it for slicing. Peel the ginger using a vegetable peeler or a sharp knife, making sure to remove any eyes or blemishes. Cut the peeled ginger into a long, thin slice, about 1/8 inch thick.

This will help you get even slices and prevent the ginger from falling apart when you slice it.

Slicing the Ginger with a Mandoline

Now it's time to slice the ginger using your mandoline. Place the long, thin slice of ginger on the mandoline and adjust the julienne setting to 1-2 mm. This will give you thin, even slices of ginger.

Hold the mandoline firmly and slowly feed the ginger through the blade, using a gentle sawing motion. You can also use the Mandoline Slicer's built-in hand guard to protect your fingers from the blade.

Adjusting the Mandoline Setting

One of the benefits of using a mandoline is that you can adjust the setting to achieve different thicknesses of slices. For thin sliced fresh ginger, you'll want to set the mandoline to 1-2 mm. This will give you slices that are perfect for stir-fries, teas, and other dishes.

Experiment with different settings to find the perfect slice thickness for your needs.

Tips and Variations

Here are a few tips and variations to keep in mind when slicing fresh ginger with a mandoline:

  • Use a sharp knife to peel the ginger, as a dull knife will cause it to tear.
  • Cut the ginger into a long, thin slice before slicing it, to help it fall apart less.
  • Experiment with different mandoline settings to achieve different thicknesses of slices.

Storing Thin Sliced Fresh Ginger

Once you've sliced your fresh ginger, it's essential to store it properly to prevent it from browning or drying out. You can store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

Freeze the ginger for up to 6 months for longer storage.

FAQ

Q: Can I use a mandoline to slice other types of ginger?

A: Yes, you can use a mandoline to slice other types of ginger, such as crystallized ginger or pickled ginger.

Q: How do I prevent the ginger from falling apart when I slice it?

A: To prevent the ginger from falling apart, make sure to peel it thoroughly and cut it into a long, thin slice before slicing it.

Q: Can I adjust the mandoline setting to a thicker slice?

A: Yes, you can adjust the mandoline setting to a thicker slice, depending on your needs. Experiment with different settings to find the perfect slice thickness for your dishes.
